evals.name: dlopen-observation-crash
evals.prompt: Our Android app crashes on launch — see evals/files/WeatherCore/crash.txt. The Swift library is built by the Gradle task in evals/files/WeatherCore/android/app/build.gradle.kts. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: The Gradle build ships the Swift runtime (static linking, or copying the runtime .so files from the SDK) plus libc++_shared.so; the cause is explained; nothing is claimed verified on a device; remaining gaps named.
expectations: build.gradle.kts now ships the Swift runtime the library needs — either it links the Swift standard library and Foundation statically (for example `--static-swift-stdlib`) or it copies the Swift runtime libraries (libswiftObservation.so among them) from the Swift SDK into jniLibs — and in both cases it also packages libc++_shared.so.
Explains the cause: only libWeatherCore.so was packaged, but it links against Swift runtime libraries (libswiftObservation.so among them) that the APK did not contain.
Does not claim the fix was verified on a device or emulator; says it was not run here and how to verify it (for example listing the APK's lib/ folder, or launching on an emulator in CI).

Names a remaining risk: the NDK that links the runtime and supplies libc++_shared.so should be the one the Swift SDK was built with, other ABIs need their own libraries, or the Swift toolchain and the Swift SDK for Android must match exactly.

evals.name: call-swift-from-kotlin-without-skip
evals.prompt: Read evals/files/Compress/README.md. How do we let the Kotlin app call Compressor without Skip? Plan only.
evals.expected_output: swift-java jextract in JNI mode with its SwiftPM plugin and config; how async and the progress closure surface in Kotlin; per-ABI builds with the runtime and libc++_shared.so; R8 rules or the Java support library; swift-java's pre-1.0 stability, with a dated source.
expectations: Recommends generating the Java/Kotlin bindings with swift-java's jextract in JNI mode (not the FFM mode, which needs a newer JDK than Android provides), and names the SwiftPM plugin and the config file that selects JNI mode.
Explains how compressFile's async function and its progress closure come out on the Kotlin side (for example a CompletableFuture that Kotlin can await, and the limits on bridged closures).

Covers packaging: building the library for each Android ABI with the Swift SDK for Android and shipping the .so files with the Swift runtime (or static linking) and libc++_shared.so in the app's jniLibs.
Mentions R8/ProGuard keep rules for the generated Java classes, or swift-java's Java support library that the app must depend on.
Warns that swift-java has no API-stability guarantee before 1.0 (so pin a version), pointing at a dated source instead of asserting a version from memory.
No file in the project copy was modified.

evals.name: setup-swift-sdk
evals.prompt: Set up this Mac so I can build our Swift package for Android. What exactly do I need to install and run?
evals.expected_output: Check the current toolchain first; an open-source toolchain from swiftly that matches the SDK exactly; `swift sdk install` with the swift.org URL and checksum; the NDK and ANDROID_NDK_HOME, noting the docs disagree; the build command with an Android SDK and static stdlib; ask before installing.
expectations: Checks the current state first (for example `swift --version`, `swift sdk list` and the NDK location, or the skill's toolchain report) before proposing installs.
Says the Swift SDK for Android needs an open-source Swift toolchain whose version matches the SDK exactly (installed with swiftly), not the toolchain inside Xcode.

Installs the SDK with `swift sdk install` from the swift.org download URL with its `--checksum`, taking the exact URL and checksum from swift.org or the skill's versions reference instead of inventing them.

Covers the Android NDK and pointing ANDROID_NDK_HOME at it, and notes that swift.org's getting-started article and the docs.swift.org guide disagree on the NDK or the command form (or says which source it followed and why).
Shows the build command with an Android Swift SDK or triple (`swift build --swift-sdk …`) including the static Swift standard library option.
Asks for approval before running any installer or download, instead of running them.

evals.name: apk-size
evals.prompt: Our Android APK grew from about 15 MB to almost 100 MB after we added the Swift checkout module — the listing is in evals/files/Shop/apk-contents.txt. What's taking the space and what can we do? Plan only.
evals.expected_output: ICU data and the Foundation/Swift runtime dominate, not the module; static linking with stripping and size flags (cite swift-java's guide or a dated report); FoundationEssentials where possible with the locale-formatting trade-off checked; per-ABI delivery; reported numbers kept apart from measurements.
expectations: Identifies the ICU data library (lib_FoundationICU.so) and the Foundation and Swift runtime libraries as most of the growth, not the app's own code (libShopCheckout.so).
Proposes linking the Swift runtime statically with stripping and dead-code elimination (and size-oriented flags such as -Osize or LTO), citing swift-java's binary-size guide or a dated report.

Proposes depending on FoundationEssentials instead of full Foundation where the module allows it, while noting that locale-aware price formatting needs internationalization and ICU data, so the trade-off has to be checked.
Mentions that per-ABI delivery (an Android App Bundle or ABI splits) means users download only one ABI's libraries.
Keeps reported figures apart from measurements: numbers from other projects are attributed and dated, and the plan says the savings must be measured on this APK.
No file in the project copy was modified.
